discovery.about: obscura-cdp, the Chrome DevTools Protocol WebSocket server: connection handling, method dispatch, per-domain handlers and a large CDP regression test suite.
discovery.see: The CDP server: /json/version, /json/list and /json/protocol discovery, WebSocket accept with a bearer token required for non-loopback binds, thread-per-connection serving capped by --max-connections, session routing, spawning long navigations and evaluations off the dispatcher, interception and events.

The CDP method router and CdpContext: maps about 77 method names to domain handlers, decides which methods may run without the per-connection V8 lock, and manages pages, sessions, targets and browser contexts.

Page domain: enable, navigate and reload with waitUntil, frame tree and child frame ids, isolated worlds, lifecycle events, scripts on new document, navigation history, layout metrics, captureScreenshot, captureSnapshot, start and stop screencast with frame acks, and printToPDF.

Runtime domain: evaluate and callFunctionOn with returnByValue and awaitPromise, getProperties with object ids, releaseObject and object groups, addBinding and removeBinding with identifier validation, console and exception events, heap usage and execution contexts.

DOM domain: getDocument, querySelector and querySelectorAll, getOuterHTML, describeNode, resolveNode, setAttributeValue, removeNode and focus, resolving nodes by nodeId, backendNodeId or objectId, plus file input MIME types.

Input domain: dispatchMouseEvent with buttons, clicks, wheel scrolling and label activation, dispatchKeyEvent and insertText with safe string escaping for generated KeyboardEvent scripts, touch events and setIgnoreInputEvents.

Accessibility domain: getFullAXTree computing roles (button, link, heading, form controls, landmarks, tables, dialogs, tabs, menus) and accessible names and visibility from the live DOM and cascade as CDP AXValue nodes.

Target domain: discovery, getTargets, createTarget, attachToTarget and attachToBrowserTarget with flattened sessions, closeTarget, auto-attach, detach, activation, browser contexts and target info including canAccessOpener.

Network domain: enable, extra HTTP headers, user agent override, setCookie, setCookies, deleteCookies and clearBrowserCookies against the session's page jar, cache disabling, request interception, blocked URLs and response bodies.
Fetch domain for request interception: enable and disable patterns, continueRequest, fulfillRequest, failRequest, getResponseBody and takeResponseBodyAsStream.
Emulation domain: setEmulatedMedia including prefers-reduced-motion, device metrics overrides and clearing them, default background color, user agent and locale overrides, and touch emulation.

DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot for DOM-agent frameworks such as browser-use: synthesizes distinct on-screen boxes, plausible computed styles and isClickable flags per node keyed by backendNodeId, so element detection works even without real layout geometry.

Render-feature implementation of Page.printToPDF: validates numeric print parameters such as paper size, margins and scale, maps them to the browser's raster PDF exporter, and returns base64 data or an IO stream handle with transferMode ReturnAsStream.
IO domain read and close for streamed results such as PDFs and response bodies (issue 360): returns base64 chunks of 1 MiB by default and at most 4 MiB per IO.read instead of the whole payload.

Storage domain cookie methods (getCookies, setCookies, clearCookies, deleteCookies) that resolve the cookie jar for a browserContextId or the session's page and reuse the Network cookie parsing and JSON conversion.
Browser domain: getVersion, close, getWindowForTarget, setDownloadBehavior and window bounds methods that Puppeteer and Playwright call during connection.

Obscura's custom LP domain with a single method, LP.getMarkdown, which evaluates the shared Markdown extraction script from obscura-js on the session's page and returns the result as a markdown string.

Parsing helpers that turn CDP cookie parameter objects into cookies (name, value, url, domain, path, secure, httpOnly, sameSite, expires) and Network.deleteCookies parameters into a typed deletion filter.
Helpers shared by CDP domain handlers, notably the file-scheme navigation detector that every navigation entrypoint uses to enforce --allow-file-access consistently.

Serde types for CDP wire messages: CdpRequest with id, method, params and optional sessionId, CdpResponse with result or CdpError, and CdpEvent for server-initiated notifications sent over the WebSocket.

Issue 19 smoke test: five parallel CDP clients each creating a target and navigating must not abort the process; related files cover heavy subresource pages, Fetch interception and per-page heap isolation over one connection.
Issues 872 and 873: concurrent pages multiplexed over one CDP connection, as Playwright connectOverCDP does, must each keep their own live JavaScript heap.
Issue 62 regression: the /json/version HTTP control plane must answer promptly even while synchronous V8 evaluation blocks the LocalSet thread that processes CDP messages.
Issue 715 regression: the single accept thread shared by all clients must survive connections that never send a request head, instead of blocking forever on a peek and refusing everyone else.
Checks that --max-connections bounds the thread-per-connection server: each connection owns an OS thread and V8 isolates, so without a cap a client could grow threads and memory without limit.
Checks that a CDP client cannot read local files without --allow-file-access through any navigation route, including the deferred Page.navigate path and page-initiated location changes.
Issue 600 protocol regression: Page.getFrameTree must list child frames and Page.frameAttached must be emitted, so Playwright and Puppeteer clients can see and address iframes.
Issue 406 regression: fetch, XHR and dynamic resource requests from page JavaScript must emit Network.requestWillBeSent and responseReceived so page.on request and response observe them.
Issue 389 regression: structured-clone primitives that bootstrap.js stubbed caused Cloudflare managed challenges to hang; each parity case fails before the fix and passes after.
Conformance parity for standard Web APIs Chrome exposes but bootstrap.js left undefined, so feature-detecting vendor scripts no longer die with not-a-function errors.
Issue 433 regression: Input.dispatchKeyEvent must escape both backslash and single quote in key and code values when interpolating them into generated KeyboardEvent scripts.
Security regression: Runtime.getProperties child object ids built from page-controlled keys must be escaped before interpolation into generated lookup scripts.
Checks that HTMLFormElement.submit() submits without firing a cancelable submit event, so a listener calling preventDefault cannot veto it, unlike requestSubmit; fixes invisible-reCAPTCHA flows.

Checks Tab key sequential focus navigation per HTML: positive tabIndex first, then document order, skipping disabled, hidden and tabindex -1 elements, with Shift reversing and canceled keydown doing nothing.

Issue 409 regression: a stylesheet link inserted by JavaScript must fetch and fire load so frameworks awaiting lazy CSS do not hang; a sibling test covers dynamic script onload after timers (issue 474).

Execution context tests: committed document contexts on new targets, page-owned default context ids, navigation of one page preserving another page's contexts, and ordered context events for every Runtime attachment.
Accessibility tree tests: accessible names come from the live DOM with stable backend node ids, labels preserve link text, and names and visibility follow the live CSS cascade.
Single entry point for the integration test binary that links the browser engine once and checks every integration test file is registered in it; nextest still runs each test in its own process.
